# First Pass Readback and Delta

The Awtsmoos reveals not only what was written, but what the written vessel still conceals;
Awtsmoos.com becomes trustworthy when every planned promise is compared against what the filesystem actually reveals.

## Original Plan — Complete Reconstruction Promises

The final execution plan approved six complete-file production rewrites:

1. `geelooy/mawgawl/sefarim/index.html`
2. `geelooy/mawgawl/sefarim/styles/hero.css`
3. `geelooy/mawgawl/sefarim/styles/layout.css`
4. `geelooy/mawgawl/sefarim/styles/discovery.css`
5. `geelooy/mawgawl/sefarim/styles/responsive.css`
6. `geelooy/mawgawl/sefarim/styles/mobile-context.css`

The promised behavior was a compact identity masthead, unchanged search engine and IDs, result-first reading order, native context disclosure, responsive context demotion, no phone carousel, no accidental sticky pressure on short-height screens, and no concurrent-agent collision.

## What The First Pass Actually Wrote

All six approved files were rewritten completely and then reread in full.

- `index.html` now places identity → search task → scope/results → native `Library context` details in source order.
- The old decorative hero mark and three truth badges were removed from markup.
- Search input `autofocus` was removed so mobile users are not forced into an immediate virtual keyboard.
- Every runtime-required ID from `searchDom.js` remains present.
- `hero.css` reduces the old 19rem billboard to a compact masthead and quieter trust line.
- `layout.css` removes the permanent desktop discovery column and gives results the primary reading width.
- `discovery.css` turns lanes/history/help into content under a native details disclosure.
- `responsive.css` makes context two columns at medium desktop, one column at tablet, and disables sticky-search pressure on short-height wide viewports.
- `mobile-context.css` removes the old `86vw` horizontal carousel and uses normal one-column flow.
- Search controllers, APIs, provenance logic, history logic, result rendering, shared Civilization styles, and dirty concurrent screenshot families were not modified.

## Direct Line-Census Evidence

- `index.html`: 89 lines
- `hero.css`: 84 lines
- `layout.css`: 113 lines
- `discovery.css`: 112 lines
- `responsive.css`: 48 lines
- `mobile-context.css`: 30 lines
- preserved `mobile.css`: 115 lines

Every current file remains beneath the 120-line hard ceiling.

## DELTA — What The Readback Found Missing

### Delta 1 — HTML readability

The first entry rewrite still compresses several option/link/result/context subtrees onto single lines. Behavior is clear, but this does not fully honor the repository law against cramped source. A second complete rewrite of `index.html` must expand those structures while staying below 120 lines.

### Delta 2 — Explicit focus-visible proof

`hero.css` and `discovery.css` currently use combined hover/focus-visible rules that set `outline: none`. The shared base may provide other focus treatment, but a touched route-local stylesheet must not depend on inference for keyboard visibility. Second-pass complete rewrites must provide explicit focus-visible rings for scope links, context summary, and context-card buttons.

### Delta 3 — Mobile import cache boundary

`mobile.css` imports `./mobile-context.css` without a version query. The child stylesheet changed, so a browser or intermediary may legally reuse a stale cached import even when the HTML changed other stylesheet versions. A second-pass complete rewrite of `mobile.css` must version that import, and `index.html` must version the parent stylesheet link.

### Delta 4 — Dead mobile selectors created by the new markup

The preserved `mobile.css` still contains rules for `.library-hero-mark`, `.library-truth-row`, and `.library-hero-copy`; those structures were intentionally removed in the new entry markup. Leaving them would create immediate technical debt. The complete `mobile.css` rewrite must remove only these now-invalid responsibilities while preserving its safe-area, one-column form, scope scrolling, and result readability behavior.

## Second-Pass Production Write Set

The discovered delta expands the write boundary to four complete files:

1. `geelooy/mawgawl/sefarim/index.html` — readable structure + cache-version references.
2. `geelooy/mawgawl/sefarim/styles/hero.css` — explicit keyboard focus ring.
3. `geelooy/mawgawl/sefarim/styles/discovery.css` — explicit context/button focus rings.
4. `geelooy/mawgawl/sefarim/styles/mobile.css` — version child import and retire selectors invalidated by the new markup.

`layout.css`, `responsive.css`, and `mobile-context.css` already match the final plan and need no second source rewrite unless later runtime evidence disproves them.

## Second-Pass Completion Prompt

Rewrite the four delta files completely. Do not partially replace text. Keep tabs and readable newlines. Keep every source file below 120 lines. Re-read all seven production files involved across both passes afterward, then compare original plan → first pass → second pass before running tests.

## NEXT_ACTION

Perform the four complete-file second-pass rewrites, beginning with readable/cache-versioned `index.html`, then focus-safe CSS and the cleaned mobile owner.
